daily_messages.title: Fulbright Application is now OPEN!
daily_messages.description: The Fulbright application is now OPEN for candidates applying for grants in the 2021-2022 cycle.  Class of 2021, your deadline is September 14 for Research / Study applications and September 21 for ETA applications. Be sure to select WILLIAMS COLLEGE as your institution.  Next step:  schedule an appointment with the Fellowships Office to discuss your application!

daily_messages.title: Preparing for Fall "Drop-In Discussions" (Part of Teach Summer)
daily_messages.description: Each Tues and Thurs for the next few weeks, Teach Summer is hosting "Drop-In Discussions" 10am-noon.  Today: What have you seen/read/heard about simultaneous/remote/in-person learning that sticks with you (for good or bad)? Please join us over Zoom!

daily_messages.title: Join Pen Pal Extravaganza to connect with isolated Berkshire residents!
daily_messages.description: CLIA community partner Northern Berkshire Community Coalition is starting a new project, the Pen Pal Extravaganza, to help connect with isolated Berkshire community members. The project is currently working on pairing willing communicators with willing receivers. If interested in participating, please fill out the PenPal Extravaganza Application: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdRmb9VfVspEoulOIPiTePpmqKSyOhmIJqGn-NSh83owRIhtA/viewform?fbclid=IwAR2u_UgPP4wv65bNwBglQ2zfYJ6YXNzCM8KtndEdbk4f0pucGjho7jlfTgQ COV's are also accepting applications from interested parties by phone at (413) 342-0376, please ask for Kenya.

daily_messages.title: The Berkshire Translation Project needs your help!
daily_messages.description: Do you speak Hatian Creole, Swahili, or Kinyarwanda? If so, we need your help! The Berkshire Translation Project is a student-led project by No Lost Generation that aims to help non-profits in the local area translate documents for immigration procedures and other related purposes. We currently need translators in the languages mentioned to help the Center for New Americans (CNAM) and the Berkshire Immigrant Center. This is a great remote volunteer opportunity! For more information or to sign up, email ephs.at.bic@gmail.com, or contact Maria Roman (unix: mjr8) or Gabriel Patenotte (unix: gep2). We hope to hear from you!
daily_messages.short_description: Do you speak Hatian Creole, Swahili, or Kinyarwanda? If so, we need your help help as a document translator for the Berkshire Translation Project!

daily_messages.title: Webinar on interventions for depression and anxiety in youth, Thursday, June 25 at 4PM
daily_messages.description: CLiA community partner Northern Berkshire Community Coalition is co-hosting a free webinar on Thursday, June 25 at 4PM, entitled Little Treatments, Big Effects. Professor of Psychology Jessica Schleider of Stony Brook University will share her promising research on brief interventions for depression and anxiety in youth. Pre-register or join here: https://collaborative.zoom.us/meeting/register/tJUrcOytqzwjH91JFuOpVFQoiUNSVDc2vcY1

daily_messages.title: Resources for Anti-Racism Work
daily_messages.description: Center for Learning in Action staff and colleagues across campus and the wider community have begun compiling this list of resources for those interested in engaging in anti-racism research and advocacy work. From learning missing history from EJI's History of Racial Injustice Calendar to creating short educational videos or podcasts using these Online Tech Resources, this list can help you get started. Additional recommendations are also welcome!!

daily_messages.title: PaperCut and Print Server Upgrade on July 1 at 6PM
daily_messages.description:
OIT will be upgrading the PaperCut and printing systems on Wednesday, July 1, at 6pm.
The upgrade should be done by 8:30pm. During the upgrade, campus printing will be unavailable.
Once the upgrade is complete, printing will resume. In rare cases, you may have to reboot your machine to re-connect your PaperCut client with the PaperCut server.
Please email dep3@williams.edu if you have questions or concerns about the process or the date/time of the upgrade.

daily_messages.title: Faculty Office Moves - Moving the Phone Extension
daily_messages.description:
There will be a login button on the phone if it has extension mobility enabled.  If you do not see login or logout and would like it enabled, please contact itsupport@williams.edu.  After hitting the login button, using the keypad, enter your short username.  The password is the last four digits of your Peoplesoft ID#.  After logging in, the phone will restart with your extension.

If you see someone else's extension on your phone, you can hit logout and you will then see the login button to proceed.  If you have any questions, please contact itsupport@williams.edu.  Thank you.
daily_messages.short_description: Faculty offices now have extension mobility on the phones which allows you to login to the phone to make it your extension. Please read full message for login details.
daily_messages.author: Terri-Lynn Hurley
